idiom_name: RSpec partial doubles (allow(obj).to receive) / scoped class reopening
implementation_notes: Ruby needs no type-compatible subclass - Meszaros notes that dynamically typed languages do not require the test double subclass step. The equivalent is a partial double: allow(TimeDisplay).to receive(:now).and_return(fixed) replaces just that method for the example and RSpec restores the original afterwards, with verify_partial_doubles checking the method name and arity against the real object; class_double/instance_double give the same guarantee for collaborators. Reopening the class inside the test (or subclassing it) is the literal descendant of the pattern, but scoped replacement is safer because the framework owns the restoration.
code_sketch:
RSpec.describe TimeDisplay do
  it "renders midnight" do
    sut = TimeDisplay.new
    allow(sut).to receive(:now).and_return(Time.at(0))
    expect(sut.get_current_time_as_html_fragment).to eq(midnight_html)
  end
end
pitfalls: allow_any_instance_of applies to every instance created while the stub is active, so it is easy to stub more than intended; stub the specific instance or inject a double instead.
Plain Ruby class reopening (`class TimeDisplay; def now; end; end`) inside a spec is not restored by RSpec's per-example lifecycle the way a partial double is; use the framework's method replacement.
Partial-double verification (verify_partial_doubles) must be enabled to catch typos in the stubbed method name, otherwise a misspelled stub silently keeps the real implementation.
